Laredo Independent School District has selected Advanced Technology Recycling (ATR) as its awarded vendor for electronics recycling and IT asset recovery, according to an announcement dated October 29, 2026. The award covers the district's request for proposals RFP 26-017, for electronic equipment recycling and related hardware or gear.

Under the arrangement, ATR will handle the retirement of surplus school technology — the classroom and office equipment that piles up as devices age out — including electronics recycling, secure data destruction, and IT asset disposition, with an emphasis on recovering value from retired assets and managing them in an environmentally responsible way.

That data-destruction piece matters for a school district: retired computers, tablets, and other devices can still hold student and staff information, so the announcement frames the work as a coordinated process for identifying data-bearing equipment, managing storage constraints during cleanouts, and disposing of aging devices responsibly rather than letting them sit in closets and warehouses.

Laredo ISD serves approximately 19,500 students across 33 educational institutions in Webb County, according to the announcement, and has served the community since 1882. The district's structured approach to surplus technology, the announcement says, reflects stewardship of public resources and attention to environmental sustainability.

Sources:

  • GlobeNewswire, "Laredo Independent School District Selects Advanced Technology Recycling for Electronics Recycling and IT Asset Recovery Program," October 29, 2026

title: Laredo ISD taps electronics-recycling vendor to retire old classroom tech securely
